## What it is

One clip, printed many times, all identical. A short sleeve snaps onto a single turn of the silicone tube. Above and below the sleeve, a stem ends in a concave saddle that cradles the neighbouring turn. The saddles are open cradles, not second snaps.

## Design notes

- Centre to centre is one pitch, `tube_od + gap`, 23 mm with the defaults. The saddle is an arc of a 13 mm circle whose crown is exactly that far from the sleeve, so the turn above and the turn below sit on the pitch.
- The cradle is shallow on purpose: about 1.2 mm deep and 7.6 mm across the arc, with a 1.2 mm flat land on each side. Deeper, and the saddle is wider than the base clip's 11.5 mm mouth, so the in-line clip on turn 2 would hit the base. The crown, not the depth, sets the spacing.
- `pad_thickness` is the radial width of the stem between the sleeve and each saddle (the vertical bar in the side view). The saddle head is wider than the stem so the arc has somewhere to sit, and still narrower than the base mouth.
- `snap_opening` is the mouth of the sleeve. 11.5 mm on a 13 mm tube. The bore itself is 0.4 mm over the tube so the LEDs are not crushed; the mouth is what holds it.
- Clips go on alternating turns, in line with the base clips. The turn between two clips sits in both saddles, and the plastic misses by about 10.6 mm. Four per clipped turn. On the 1000 mm strip that is turns 2 and 4, eight clips.
- The sleeve, the mouth, and both saddles are swept on the helix. Over the 14 mm band the centreline bows 0.72 mm toward the coil centre and rises 1.52 mm. A straight extrusion made the tube take that bend instead.
- Prints on one helical end. That end is flat on the bed because it is perpendicular to the tube there. The band then leans at most 15 degrees, which is the helix turning through the clip. The part is 16 mm tall.
- The 0.6 mm chamfer on the upper end meets the saddle land and leaves four tiny faces. They are the chamfer, not a stray flake.

```toml
[accepted]
sliver = 4
```

## Don't

- Don't extrude this band straight. The bore and the saddles have to follow the helix or the tube is forced straight for 14 mm.
- Don't put a clip on every turn. The top saddle of one and the bottom saddle of the next would occupy the same gap.
- Don't rotate alternate turns by 45 degrees. Tom's clips line up with the base. The unclipped turn between them is what keeps the stacked clips apart.
- Don't close the saddles into snaps. They only cradle. The sleeve is the only snap.
- Don't stretch the saddle out to a deeper arc without widening the base mouth first. The turn-2 saddle has to drop into that mouth.
